meta.title: 02.Sentence Analysis - Advanced (C1-C2)
meta.description: A comprehensive 60-question intermediate error identification test featuring varied sentence structures, diverse grammar topics, and contexts relatable to Indonesian learners.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause). Click on the error(s) and type the correction. Choose No Error if correct.
questions.sentence: Last summer, my family and I travel to Bali, where we stayed at a beautiful resort near the beach and enjoyed delicious local food.
questions.explanation: Topic: Past Simple Tense. The time marker 'Last summer' indicates a completed action in the past, so the verb must be in the past simple form 'traveled', not the present form 'travel'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The university students in Bandung does not has enough time to study because they are working part-time jobs every weekend.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement. The subject 'students' is plural, so it requires the plural auxiliary 'do' and the base verb 'have', not the singular 'does' and 'has'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Rendang is a traditional Indonesian dish that originates from West Sumatra and is famous worldwide for its rich and spicy flavor.
questions.explanation: Topic: General Grammar and Vocabulary. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present simple tense for general facts and maintains proper parallel structure.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If you want to avoid the heavy traffic in Jakarta, you should to take the commuter line train early in the morning.
questions.explanation: Topic: Modal Verbs. Modal verbs like 'should' are always followed directly by the base form of the verb without 'to'. Therefore, 'should take' is correct.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: She have bought a new laptop online yesterday, but it arrive damaged and the seller refuse to give a full refund.
questions.explanation: Topic: Past Simple Tense. The time marker 'yesterday' requires all verbs in the sequence of past events to be in the past simple form: 'bought', 'arrived', and 'refused'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: During the rainy season, it is important to bringing an umbrella when you go outside, because the weather can change very quickly.
questions.explanation: Topic: Infinitives. The structure 'it is important to' must be followed by the base form of the verb (the to-infinitive), so 'bring' is correct, not the gerund 'bringing'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Many tech startups in Indonesia are developing innovative applications to help local farmers sell their products directly to consumers.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Continuous and Relative Clauses. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present continuous for ongoing actions and a relative clause ('which improves') to add extra information.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The doctor advised him to drinks plenty of water and get enough rest if he wants to recover from the flu quickly.
questions.explanation: Topic: Infinitives after Verbs. The verb 'advise' is followed by an object and a to-infinitive ('advised him to drink'). The 'to' must be followed by the base form 'drink', not 'drinks'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Although she studied very hardly for the final exam, she didn't passed because she was too nervous during the test.
questions.explanation: Topic: Adverbs and Past Simple Negatives. 'Hard' is both an adjective and an adverb; 'hardly' means 'almost not'. Also, after the auxiliary 'didn't', the verb must be in its base form 'pass'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: We are looking forward to visit the new high-speed railway station in Jakarta next month with our relatives.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds after Prepositions. In the phrase 'look forward to', the word 'to' is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. Therefore, it must be followed by a gerund ('visiting').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The traditional batik fabric is made using a complex process that involves applying hot wax to the cloth before dyeing it with natural colors.
questions.explanation: Topic: Passive Voice and Gerunds. No error. The sentence correctly uses the passive voice ('is made') and follows the verb 'involves' with a gerund ('applying').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My brother have been working as a software engineer at a prominent company in South Jakarta since he graduated last year.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect Continuous. The singular subject 'My brother' requires the singular auxiliary 'has', not 'have', to form the present perfect continuous tense.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If I will have enough money next year, I would travel to Japan to experience the cherry blossom season and try authentic sushi.
questions.explanation: Topic: First Conditional. In a first conditional sentence (real future possibility), the 'if' clause uses the present simple ('have'), and the main clause uses the future simple ('will travel').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The teacher explained that the earth go around the sun, which is a basic fact that every student should know.
questions.explanation: Topic: Reported Speech and General Truths. Even in reported speech, general truths or scientific facts remain in the present simple tense. The singular subject 'earth' requires 'goes'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Despite the heavy rain, the outdoor music festival in Bandung continued as planned, and the audience enjoyed the performance very much.
questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctions and Past Simple. No error. 'Despite' is correctly used as a preposition followed by a noun phrase, and the past simple verbs are used correctly.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: One of the most popular tourist destination in Indonesia is the island of Bali, which attracts millions of visitors annually.
questions.explanation: Topic: Superlatives and Plural Nouns. The structure 'one of the' must always be followed by a plural noun ('destinations'), as it refers to a single item within a larger group.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: She is used to wake up early every morning because she have to catch the first bus to her office in the city center.
questions.explanation: Topic: 'Be used to' and Subject-Verb Agreement. 'Be used to' expresses a habit and is followed by a gerund ('waking'). Also, the singular subject 'she' requires 'has', not 'have'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The new shopping mall in Surabaya offers a wide variety of international brands, making it a favorite spot for teenagers who loves to hang out.
questions.explanation: Topic: Relative Clauses and Subject-Verb Agreement. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural noun 'teenagers', so the verb must be plural ('love'), not singular ('loves').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: After finishing her homework, the student decided to read a novel about Indonesian history before going to sleep early that night.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds and Infinitives. No error. The sentence correctly uses a gerund after the preposition 'After' and an infinitive after the verb 'decided'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Neither the manager nor the employees was happy with the new policy regarding remote work arrangements that was introduced last month.
questions.explanation: Topic: Correlative Conjunctions and Agreement. With 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'employees' is plural, the verb must be 'were'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I have never been to Yogyakarta, but my friends told me that the culture there are very rich and the people is friendly.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement. 'Culture' is a singular noun requiring 'is'. 'People' is a plural noun requiring 'are'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The government has built several new bridges to connect the remote islands, making transportation much more easier for the locals.
questions.explanation: Topic: Comparatives. 'Easier' is already the comparative form of 'easy'. Adding 'more' creates an incorrect double comparative. Use 'much easier'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: If you heat water to one hundred degrees Celsius, it boils and turns into steam, which is a basic scientific principle.
questions.explanation: Topic: Zero Conditional. No error. The zero conditional (present simple + present simple) is correctly used to express a general truth or scientific fact.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The documentary about the Komodo dragon were broadcasted on national television last night and received excellent reviews.
questions.explanation: Topic: Passive Voice and Irregular Verbs. The singular subject 'documentary' requires 'was'. The past participle of 'broadcast' is 'broadcast', not 'broadcasted'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Although he was feeling very tired, but he continued to working on his project until midnight to meet the deadline.
questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctions and Infinitives. 'Although' and 'but' cannot be used in the same sentence. Also, 'continue' is followed by a to-infinitive ('to work'), not a gerund.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: There are many informations available on the internet about how to prepare authentic Indonesian dishes at home.

correctAnswers: There is a lot of information

questions.explanation: Topic: Uncountable Nouns. 'Information' is an uncountable noun. It cannot be pluralized with an 's' and must be used with a singular verb ('is') and quantifiers like 'much' or 'a lot of'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The local community has successfully preserved the ancient temple, ensuring that future generations can learn about their cultural heritage.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Participles. No error. The present perfect ('has preserved') is correctly used for an action with present relevance, followed by a participle clause ('ensuring').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: She asked me where did I buy my new backpack, and I told her that I got it from a local artisan.
questions.explanation: Topic: Indirect Questions. In an embedded or indirect question, the word order must be subject + verb ('I bought'), not the inverted question form ('did I buy').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The prices of the flight tickets to Lombok is getting more expensive, so we decides to cancel our trip.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement and Past Simple. The plural subject 'prices' requires the plural verb 'are'. The narrative is in the past, so 'decided' is correct, not 'decides'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My father has been driving the same car for over ten years, and it still runs very smoothly despite its old age.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Simple for Facts/Habits. The singular pronoun 'it' (referring to the car) requires the third-person singular verb 'runs' in the present simple tense.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Before you submit the application form, please make sure that you have filled in all the required details correctly.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Imperatives. No error. The sentence correctly uses an imperative ('please make sure') followed by a present perfect clause ('have filled') to indicate a completed action.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The children were playing football in the park when suddenly it started to raining heavily and they had to run home.
questions.explanation: Topic: Infinitives. The verb 'start' can be followed by a to-infinitive ('to rain') or a gerund ('raining'), but not both together ('to raining').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I am agree with your opinion about the new school rules, because they is too strict and unfair to the students.
questions.explanation: Topic: Stative Verbs and Subject-Verb Agreement. 'Agree' is a verb, so 'I agree' is correct (not 'I am agree'). The plural pronoun 'they' requires the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the movie already started, so we missed the first twenty minutes of the film.

multiErrorSegments.text: to wait for the next show.

questions.explanation: Topic: Past Perfect Tense. When two actions happen in the past, the action that happened first requires the past perfect tense ('had already started') to show the sequence clearly.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The chef recommended trying the spicy noodle soup, which is a signature dish of the restaurant and very popular among locals.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds and Relative Clauses. No error. 'Recommend' is correctly followed by a gerund ('trying'), and the relative clause is properly structured.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Every morning, the street vendors sets up their carts near the station to sell breakfast to the commuters.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement. The plural subject 'vendors' requires the plural verb 'set', not the singular 'sets', in the present simple tense.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: She is the woman which won the national writing competition last year, and her book are now a bestseller.
questions.explanation: Topic: Relative Pronouns and Subject-Verb Agreement. Use 'who' for people, not 'which'. The singular subject 'book' requires the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: We should to respect the local customs and traditions when we visit a new village or a different region of the country.
questions.explanation: Topic: Modal Verbs. Modal verbs like 'should' are followed directly by the base form of the verb without 'to'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The library provides a quiet environment for students to study, and it also offers free access to a wide range of digital resources.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Simple and Infinitives. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present simple for facts and the to-infinitive to express purpose.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If I was you, I would accept the job offer immediately because it is a great opportunity for your career.
questions.explanation: Topic: Second Conditional (Subjunctive). In hypothetical 'if' clauses, 'were' is used for all subjects, including 'I', 'he', 'she', and 'it'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The amount of people who attended the concert was surprisingly large, and many of them was disappointed by the sound quality.
questions.explanation: Topic: Quantifiers and Subject-Verb Agreement. 'Number' is used for countable nouns ('people'), while 'amount' is for uncountable nouns. 'Many of them' is plural and requires 'were'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The museum exhibition features several ancient artifacts that was discovered in the rural areas of Central Java.
questions.explanation: Topic: Relative Clauses and Passive Voice. The relative pronoun 'that' refers to the plural noun 'artifacts', so the passive verb must be plural ('were discovered').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: Although the hike to the top of the mountain was challenging, the breathtaking view made the entire effort completely worthwhile.
questions.explanation: Topic: Conjunctions and Past Simple. No error. 'Although' correctly introduces a concessive clause, and the past simple verbs are used appropriately.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My sister is good at playing the piano, and she has been taking lessons since she is five years old.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Past Simple. The main clause uses present perfect continuous ('has been taking'), but the 'since' clause refers to a specific completed point in the past, requiring the past simple ('was').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: He didn't knew the answer to the difficult question, so he asked his classmate to helps him understand the topic.
questions.explanation: Topic: Past Simple Negatives and Infinitives. After the auxiliary 'didn't', the verb must be in its base form ('know'). Similarly, 'to' is followed by the base form ('help').

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The company is planning to open a new branch in Medan, which will create hundreds of new job opportunity for the local residents.
questions.explanation: Topic: Countable Nouns. 'Hundreds of' indicates a plural quantity, so the countable noun 'opportunity' must be pluralized to 'opportunities'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The traditional market is always bustling with activity early in the morning, offering fresh produce and a vibrant atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Simple and Participles. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present simple for a habitual state and a participle ('offering') to add descriptive detail.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I wish I can speak English fluently, because it would help me communicate better with international colleagues.
questions.explanation: Topic: 'Wish' Clauses. To express a wish about a present or future situation that is currently untrue or unlikely, we use the past simple or 'could' after 'wish'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The police has arrested the suspect who steal the motorcycle from the parking area yesterday afternoon.
questions.explanation: Topic: Collective Nouns and Past Simple. 'Police' is a plural collective noun requiring 'have'. The time marker 'yesterday' requires the past simple 'stole'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: Despite of the strong wind, the fishermen decided to go out to sea to catch enough fish for the market.
questions.explanation: Topic: Prepositions and Conjunctions. 'Despite' is a preposition and should not be followed by 'of'. The correct forms are either 'Despite' or 'In spite of'.

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The university library is open until late at night, providing students with a comfortable space to prepare for their upcoming examinations.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Simple and Participles. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present simple for a current state and a participle clause ('providing') to show result or additional information.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The manager told the employees that they must to finish the report by the end of the week.
questions.explanation: Topic: Modal Verbs. Modal verbs like 'must' are followed directly by the base form of the verb without 'to'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: My parents gave me many good advices about how to manage my money and saving for the future.

correctAnswers: a lot of good advice about

questions.explanation: Topic: Uncountable Nouns and Parallelism. 'Advice' is uncountable and cannot take an 's' or 'many'. Also, 'to manage' and 'save' must be parallel infinitives.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The new bridge connecting the two islands are expected to be completed by the end of next year.
questions.explanation: Topic: Subject-Verb Agreement. The true subject is the singular noun 'bridge', not the plural 'islands'. Therefore, the verb must be singular ('is expected').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: When the power went out suddenly, the students continued their discussion by the light of their mobile phones.
questions.explanation: Topic: Past Simple and Phrasal Verbs. No error. The sentence correctly uses the past simple tense and the phrasal verb 'went out' appropriately.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: She has lived in Jakarta since five years, and she has made many good friends in the city.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Prepositions of Time. 'For' is used to indicate a duration of time ('five years'), while 'since' is used for a specific starting point in the past.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: The teacher asked the students to not talk during the exam, but some of them was still whispering to each other.
questions.explanation: Topic: Negative Infinitives and Subject-Verb Agreement. The negative infinitive is formed by placing 'not' before 'to' ('not to talk'). 'Some of them' is plural and requires 'were'.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: I am looking forward to meet you at the conference next week to discuss our potential collaboration.
questions.explanation: Topic: Gerunds after Prepositions. In the phrase 'look forward to', the word 'to' is a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund ('meeting').

questions.question: Check for errors.
questions.sentence: The local government has implemented a new recycling program to reduce waste and protect the environment for future generations.
questions.explanation: Topic: Present Perfect and Infinitives of Purpose. No error. The sentence correctly uses the present perfect for a recent action with present results, and to-infinitives to express purpose.

questions.question: Identify all errors (word, phrase, or clause).
questions.sentence: If it will rain tomorrow, the outdoor ceremony will be moved to the main hall of the building.
questions.explanation: Topic: First Conditional. In a first conditional sentence, the 'if' clause uses the present simple tense ('rains'), not the future tense ('will rain').
